title: Auth: the console cannot withdraw an authorized AI assistant: /oauth2/delete-consent has no ledger row or client method, and no admin door
body:
domain:ui#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibxW6qraU2Z3mwupUGp

Filing gate: ③ the maintainer's order that names this work: #30894 (「都同意，立卡」, 2026-11-06), whose Expected asks for "a Revoke action … An administrator can see and revoke them for a person they manage", and whose triage audit 6682129286 says the server door the page needs, if one is missing, is filed to `domain:server` first. The withdraw itself is the maintainer's cloud#3606 ruling A (「撤销或撤回时删掉这条记录 … 控制台的撤回也随之真正生效」), quoted in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.ts`. ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade and the lane. Suggested grade: p1 (#30894's grade; it is the half its Revoke needs).

**Business reason.** The consent page promises 「您可以随时在账户设置中撤销访问权限。」. Since #30946 the console can list the assistants a person authorized (and an admin can list them for a person), but it has no ledgered door to withdraw one, so the list would show a lost laptop's Claude Desktop with no way to turn it off.

**Reader.** The `domain:server` seat (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`: the route ledger, the client, an admin door), then the `domain:ui` seat holding #30894.

**Dedupe.** `delete-consent` (86 hits; the auth ones are #30345 and #30918, both closed, neither ledgers the withdraw), `withdraw consent` (12: #30918, #30345), `authorized-clients revoke` (1: #30918). **New.**

## What is on `origin/main` `115a43ad16`

- `POST /api/v1/auth/oauth2/delete-consent` is published by better-auth (`BETTER_AUTH_MOUNTED_SURFACE`, `auth-route-ledger.ts` ~L430) but has **no `AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER` row** and **no `@objectstack/client` method**. Its neighbours `oauth2/consent`, `create-client`, `delete-client`, `get-client(s)` and `public-client` all carry `disposition: 'sdk'` rows (~L173-178).
- `mcp-token-revocation.ts` already names it "the Console's withdraw": it deletes the consent row, and since #30879 `mcpConsentAdmits` refuses the token on its next request. So the effect is there; the door the console may call is not.
- The client's `oauth.authorizedClients.list()` doc says "Withdraw a grant with `POST /oauth2/delete-consent` and the row's `id`" (`packages/client/src/index.ts` ~L5006), pointing at an unledgered route.
- An administrator: `GET /api/v1/auth/admin/authorized-clients?userId=` (#30946) lists a person's grants, but nothing withdraws one for them; `delete-consent` acts for the session user only.

## Wanted

- [ ] A ledgered, client-exposed withdraw of one of the session user's own authorized assistants, by the row `id` `authorized-clients` answers (the lane picks: ledger `delete-consent` as `sdk`, or an ObjectStack mount beside `authorized-clients`). After it, that assistant's token is refused on its next MCP call.
- [ ] The same withdraw for a person a platform administrator manages, behind the same gate as `admin/authorized-clients` (security#1's rules on #30918), refused for anyone else with one indistinguishable answer.
- [ ] Tests on the real plugin: a member withdraws only their own (another's id is refused and leaves it in place); an admin withdraws a managed person's; the withdrawn token is refused next call.

Unblocks: the Revoke half of #30894. Related: #30918 (PR #30946), #30345 (PR #30879), cloud#3606.
